text:
Nina Park: Filing this here because the new next-eval-stub sample is failing parity in the eval harness for embeddings. Looks like JS SDK returns a different shape and non-deterministic vectors vs Python.

Nina Park: Repro (local): clone examples/next-eval-stub, yarn, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run yarn test:e2e. Fails in embeddings parity test where expected vector equals fixture but actual differs on a few dims.

Omar Velez: I saw a TypeScript compile error in the starter too: TS2345 on import type mismatch. Error: "Type 'number[][]' is not assignable to type 'Float32Array[]'". Our JS SDK historically returned arrays of numbers; new TS types expect typed arrays.

Priya Singh: The eval harness compares absolute values, not cosine similarity, so tiny float noise triggers a regression. Is JS SDK doing any extra normalization or using Math.random for sampling seeds? Embeddings should be deterministic for same model+input.

Nina Park: snippet from examples/api/embeds.js:```js
const res = await redwood.embeddings.create({ input: text });
// res.data[0].embedding -> [[0.1,0.2,...]] vs expected [0.1,0.2,...]
```

Theo Martin: root causes I've seen: 1) JS SDK wrapped underlying tensor backend and returns nested arrays for batched responses; Python flattens single-item batches. 2) JS RNG is unseeded for some ops in the browser shim causing tiny diffs. 3) TS defs were tightened in a recent PR to typed arrays.

Priya Singh: For the eval failure we should do two things: relax harness comparator to use cosine similarity threshold OR make JS outputs identical to Python shape + deterministic floats. I prefer fixing SDK parity so consumer code is simpler.

Omar Velez: Proposed fixes: a) SDK: coerce single-item batched embeddings to a plain number[] if batch length === 1; keep typed-array option behind a flag. b) Add optional seed param to embeddings.create({ input, seed }) which, when provided, uses a deterministic RNG path in JS native code. c) Loosen TS types to allow number[][] | Float32Array[] until we ship typed arrays fully.

Nina Park: I can submit two small PRs in examples: 1) update tests to use cosine similarity with threshold 1e-6 so we don't get noisy flakes during rollout; 2) update sample app to accept either shape (handle nested array). But core SDK fixes should land first.

Theo Martin: I'll prototype a deterministic path for the JS embedder. It will accept seed and use a seeded xorshift to produce identical floats across Node versions. We need to document that seeded mode is for eval & debugging only and may be slower.

devex-bot: CI flagged: https://ci.internal.redwood/gh/examples/next-eval-stub/34 -> tests/eval/embeddings -> 1765432150

Priya Singh: small caution: when adding seed param, ensure we don't change production default semantics (no seed => same non-deterministic runtime as today). Also update SDK docs and types.

Omar Velez: I'll open a small types PR that unions the shapes and adds a migration note in CHANGELOG: allow number[][] | Float32Array[] and add util normalizeEmbeddings() in SDK helpers.

Nina Park: thanks. I'll land the example test tolerance change in a follow-up so CI unblocks quickly. Then we can iterate on SDK patches.

Theo Martin: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/201 implementing seed option + batching normalization + unit tests. Marked as WIP.

Priya Singh: once PR is up, let's run the eval harness fixture that forces identical inputs and verify parity with python baseline. If green, flip the harness comparator back to strict equality for a limited canary.

Nina Park: created example PR to handle both shapes and add a README note for local dev about forcing deterministic mode: set REDWOOD_EMBED_SEED=42. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/88

devex-bot: PRs opened referenced above and CI jobs queued: js-sdk#201, examples#88 -> 1765432160

Omar Velez: thanks team. This explains a bunch of onboarding confusion from a few users who expected typed arrays and deterministic eval outputs. We'll follow up with a small DX note in the sample app template about the embedding shape and how to opt into typed arrays.

Nina Park: excellent. closing loop once CI passes. If anyone hits a new parity failure, ping me and I'll rerun harness with debug flags.
